verifications.claim: Generation Z was born between 1997 and 2012.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'with the generation typically being defined as people born from 1997 to 2012.[1]' 'Pew Research Center specifies that 1997 is the starting birth year for Generation Z... used 2012 as a tentative endpoint'; R4: 'Generation Z – born 1997-2012'; R8: 'specific year range of 1997–2012'; R12: 'Gen Z: ... born between 1997 and 2012'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state or cite the exact birth year range of 1997-2012 for Generation Z, matching the claim precisely.

verifications.claim: As of 2026, Generation Z is aged 14–29 years old.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 cited snippet: 'By 2026, Gen Z will be between 14 and 29 years old'; R1: birth years 1997-2012 logically yield ages 14-29 in 2026 (2026-2012=14, 2026-1997=29); R5: 'Gen Z generally includes people born between 1997 and 2012. In 2026, that makes them about 14 to 29 years old'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement in cited snippet and logical derivation from confirmed birth years in R1 exactly match the age range for 2026.

verifications.claim: Nearly 50% of Generation Z are racial/ethnic minorities in the U.S.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '50.9% of Generation Z is white...'; R7: 'Gen Z will be the last generation that is a majority white — just barely, with 51%'; R8: 'Nearly 50 percent of Gen Zers are racial and ethnic minorities'
verifications.reasoning: R1 data shows 50.9% white (thus ~49% non-white minorities); R7 and R8 explicitly state nearly 50% minorities in US context, directly supporting the claim.

verifications.claim: 16% of Generation Z identify as part of the LGBTQ+ community
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'According to a 2021 Gallup survey, 20.8%, or about one in five members, of Gen Z identify as LGBTQ+'; R8: '16 percent of Gen Zers identify as part of the LGBTQ+ community themselves'
verifications.reasoning: Sources provide conflicting figures (20.8% in R1 Gallup survey vs. 16% in R8), both in US context, creating direct contradiction on the exact percentage.
